jp_verse: 粗い器に　朝の光\n\n    飾らぬものほど　手になじむ
en_verse: Morning light rests\nupon the rough bowl—\nthe plainest things fit the hand best.

jp_verse: 夕暮れの村に　煙が昇り\n\n    小さな窓から　灯りがこぼれる
en_verse: Smoke rises softly\nabove the evening village—\nwarm light spills from tiny windows.

jp_verse: 向かい合う手に\n\n    言葉より深い　静けさがある
en_verse: Between joined hands\nrests a silence\ndeeper than words.

jp_verse: 古い机に　紙をひらけば\n\n    静かな時が　また動き出す
en_verse: Opening papers\nupon the old desk—\nquiet time begins moving again.

jp_verse: 開かれた頁に　午後の光\n\n    遠い誰かの声が　まだ残る
en_verse: Afternoon light\nfalls on the open pages—\na distant voice still lingers there.

jp_verse: 名もない服に　小さな札\n\n    誰かの記憶だけが　残されている
en_verse: A small tag hangs\nfrom the nameless dress—\nonly memory remains attached.

jp_verse: 壁の暦は　静かに減り\n\n    机の紙だけが　積もってゆく
en_verse: The wall calendar\nquietly loses days—\nonly the papers continue to gather.

jp_verse: まだ来ぬ未来へ\n\n    小さな約束が　差し出される
en_verse: Toward an unseen future\na small promise\nis gently offered.

jp_verse: 乾いた大地に　風だけが吹き\n\n    遠い雲さえ　立ち止まらない
en_verse: Across the parched earth\nonly the wind continues—\neven the clouds do not remain.

jp_verse: 細い枝先に　春は眠り\n\n    まだ名もない日を　待っている
en_verse: Spring sleeps quietly\nwithin the thin branches—\nwaiting for unnamed days.

jp_verse: 空へ伸びる　細い梢\n\n    終わりの先にも　光は続く
en_verse: The narrow treetop\nreaches into the sky—\nlight continues beyond the end.

jp_verse: 白く霞んだ　木々のあいだ\n\n    答えは　まだ姿を見せない
en_verse: Between pale trees\nblurred in the distance—\nthe answer still hides itself.

jp_verse: 水しぶきだけが　陽を砕き\n\n    夏の声が　一瞬ひらく
en_verse: A burst of water\nshatters the sunlight—\nsummer opens for a moment.

jp_verse: 湯気の向こうに　静かな食卓\n\n    懐かしさだけが　先に届く
en_verse: Beyond the rising steam\nrests a quiet table—\nmemory arrives before taste.

jp_verse: 小さな手を引く　秋の道\n\n    背中に残るのは　やさしい時間
en_verse: Along the autumn road\na small hand is held—\ngentle time remains behind them.

jp_verse: 海に浮かぶ　朱の鳥居\n\n    夕空までも　静かに染まる
en_verse: The vermilion gate\nstands upon the water—\neven the evening sky is dyed red.

jp_verse: 切り株の上に　若芽が伸びる\n\n    終わりのあとにも　命は残る
en_verse: From the old stump\na green shoot rises—\nlife remains after endings.

jp_verse: やわらかな芽が　風に揺れて\n\n    世界は　まだ始まったばかり
en_verse: The tender sprout\nsways within the wind—\nthe world has only just begun.

jp_verse: 草原を渡る　淡い風\n\n    名もない命が　静かに光る
en_verse: A pale breeze crosses\nthe field of grass—\nnameless lives glow quietly.

jp_verse: 強い風に　草は伏しても\n\n    根だけは　土を離れない
en_verse: Though the harsh wind\nbends the grass low—\nits roots never leave the earth.
